name: zone-planner-drag
description: Zone Planner pan and paint strokes driven by a REAL mouse. The planner asks the window system whether the pan's or stroke's button is still down (GLFW below 26.3, SDL on 26.3), which the bridge's synthetic events cannot fake, so this scenario only sets the screen up and waits while a person or a desktop-control agent drives the map (an agent sends right through scripts/smoke/Send-MouseButton.ps1; see the README): first 45 s with an empty hand (hold LEFT, drag, release: the map pans), then, with the red brush on the cursor, 90 s for a stroke (hold LEFT, drag, tap RIGHT while still holding left, keep dragging, release LEFT). The red layer is echoed before and after. Expected: the map follows the pan drag; one red rectangle from the press point to the release point; a rectangle that stops where right was tapped, or nothing at all, is the bug. A plain right-drag erases the same way. Run it on 1.21.1 (GLFW, oldest), 26.2 and 26.3 (SDL).

steps.label: window 1600x900 (the map spans the left of the screen at guiScale 3)
park the cursor off the map

steps.name: zp-start
steps.look: the Zone Planner map at its opening view

steps.label: REAL MOUSE NOW (pan): empty hand, hold LEFT on the map, drag about a third of its width, release
park the cursor off the map

steps.name: zp-panned
steps.look: the map shifted the way the cursor was dragged (the terrain moved with the cursor)

steps.label: red layer before (expect no painted entries)
park the cursor off the map

steps.name: zp-before
steps.look: the Zone Planner map, red brush on the cursor, nothing painted

steps.label: REAL MOUSE NOW (paint): on the map hold LEFT, drag, tap RIGHT (left still held), keep dragging, release LEFT

steps.name: zp-after
steps.look: one red rectangle from where left went down to where it came up (not cut short where right was tapped)

steps.label: remove the planner (its layers live in the block entity)
